discovery: Prediction and experimental discovery of the spin Hall effect

nominees.name: David D. Awschalom
nominees.affiliation: University of Chicago and Argonne National Laboratory, USA

nominees.name: Tomas Jungwirth
nominees.affiliation: Institute of Physics, Czech Academy of Sciences, Prague, Czech Republic

motivation: Dyakonov (with the late V. I. Perel) predicted in 1971 that spin-orbit coupling causes an electric current to produce a transverse spin current, which builds up spin at the edges of a conductor. For three decades the idea stayed on paper. In 2004–2005 Awschalom's group used Kerr-rotation microscopy to image spin accumulation in GaAs. In parallel, Jungwirth and co-workers detected it with electroluminescence in two-dimensional hole systems, and Jungwirth went on to lead much of the theory. Several groups have since reproduced the result many times over. The spin Hall effect and its inverse are now the standard way to generate and detect pure spin currents. They underlie spin-orbit torque switching in magnetic memory, spin pumping and spin caloritronics, and the field of antiferromagnetic and altermagnetic spintronics. This is a clear case of a general theoretical principle that was confirmed by experiment and has reorganized an entire field.
